momentum_note: The trend is accelerating sharply. Producers with hedging infrastructure and pricing-power contracts (CF, Glencore, Ball, Crown) are systematizing the transfer of commodity volatility downstream to non-hedged counterparties. Cleveland-Cliffs and Commercial Metals show the lag effect: they absorbed fixed-price automotive contracts through weak periods and now lag recovery. Glencore's marketing arm turning +142% YoY shows how disruption becomes a designed profit engine for the integrated. The trend is not cyclical friction; it is contractually embedded asymmetry that sharpens when prices move.
